influenza: An acute contagious disease of the upper airways and lungs, caused by a virus, which rapidly spreads around the world in seasonal epidemics.
motorist: One who drives a motor vehicle.
transgression: A violation of a law, duty or commandment.
guardianship: The office or position of one acting as a guardian or conservator, especially in a legal capacity.
firmament: (usually uncountable) The vault of the heavens, where the clouds, sun, moon, and stars can be seen; the heavens, the sky.
blatantly: In a blatant manner; so as to be highly visible or obvious.
draught: A current of air, usually coming into a room or vehicle.
juggler: Agent noun of juggle; one who either literally juggles objects, or figuratively juggles tasks.
fenders: Panel of a car which encloses the wheel area, especially the front wheels
beheld: To see or look at, esp. appreciatively; to descry, look upon.
lunge: A sudden forward movement, especially with a sword.
patchouli: Any of several East Indian plants in the genus Pogostemon, especially Pogostemon cablin, which yield a highly fragrant oil.
tutorial: A self-paced learning exercise; a lesson prepared so that a student can learn at their own speed, at their convenience.
brokenhearted: Grieved and disappointed, especially with the loss of a beloved person or thing, such as the repudiation of a romantic relationship.
glade: An open passage through a wood; a grassy open or cleared space in a forest.
mounds: An artificial hill or elevation of earth; a raised bank; an embankment thrown up for defense
plucky: Having or showing pluck, courage or spirit in trying circumstances.
gangplank: A board used as a temporary footbridge between a ship and a dockside.
millennia: A period of time consisting of one thousand years.
propriety: The particular character or essence of someone or something; individuality.
simulations: Something that simulates a system or environment in order to predict actual behaviour.
windfall: Something that has been blown down by the wind.
destinations: The act of destining or appointing.
forts: A fortified defensive structure stationed with troops.
kickbacks: A backward kick, a retrograde movement of an extremity.
playgrounds: (outdoors) A large open space for children to play on, usually having dedicated play equipment (such as swings and slides).
swum: To move through the water, without touching the bottom; to propel oneself in water by natural means.
cordless: Having no cord; especially using batteries instead of mains electricity
handguns: A small gun with a relatively short barrel, designed to be held and operated with a single hand.
organizers: A person who arranges the details of a public event.
strapless: Without a strap or straps; usually describing women's clothing without shoulder straps.
hotdog: A sandwich consisting of a frankfurter, or wiener, in a bread roll, usually served with ketchup, mustard, relish, etc.
perturbed: To disturb; to bother or unsettle.
urinary: A urinary device or fixture: a urinal.
griffins: A mythical beast having the body of a lion and the wings and head of an eagle.
tulle: A kind of silk lace or light netting, used for clothing, veils, etc.
oscillator: A tuned electronic circuit used to generate a continuous output waveform.
inoculate: To introduce an antigenic substance or vaccine into something (e.g. the body) or someone, such as to produce immunity to a specific disease.
jibe: A facetious or insulting remark; a jeer, a taunt.
mendacity: The fact or condition of being untruthful; dishonesty.
moloch: Moloch horridus, an Australian lizard thought to be the sole member of the genus Moloch.
bookshelf: A shelf or shelves for storing books for easy visual reference.
feminism: The state of being feminine; femininity.
intervening: To become involved in a situation, so as to alter or prevent an action.
chessboard: The square board used in the game of chess, subdivided into eight rows of eight squares each, the squares in each row and column being of alternating colours.
hunker: To crouch or squat close to the ground or lie down
calypso: A type of music and dance that originated in the West Indies (perhaps Trinidad), characterized by improvised lyrics on topical or broadly humorous subjects, often creating satire of current events.
familia: (Roman law) The paterfamilias, his legitimate descendants and their wives, and all persons adopted into his family and their wives.
odors: Any smell, whether fragrant or offensive.
underhand: The lower of two hands, the hand under the work.
paddock: A small enclosure or field of grassland, especially for horses.
rancheros: (of Mexico) A rancher or herdsman; a peasant employed on a ranch or rancho.
poppet: (term of endearment) An endearingly sweet or beautiful child.
pedicures: Superficial cosmetic treatment of the feet and toenails.
baklava: A popular sweet pastry found in many cuisines of the Middle East and the Balkans, made of chopped nuts layered with phyllo pastry.
inns: Any establishment where travellers can procure lodging, food, and drink.
schoolbooks: A textbook, a book used, or prepared for use, in school.
electrode: The terminal through which electric current passes between metallic and nonmetallic parts of an electric circuit
rigatoni: A ribbed tubular form of pasta, larger than penne but with square-cut ends, often slightly curved.
manta: A kind of fabric or blanket used in Latin America and southwestern United States.
amulets: A kind of protective charm or ornament, often bearing magical symbols, worn for protection against ill will, negative influences or evil spirits.
guilders: One who gilds; especially one whose occupation is to overlay things with gold.
treetops: The crown or uppermost branches of a tree
cheekbone: The small prominent bone of the cheek.
elocution: The art of public speaking with expert control of gesture and voice, etc.
hearties: A term of familiar address and fellowship among sailors.
pecks: An act of striking with a beak.
regrouping: To pause and get organized before trying again.
thimble: A pitted, now usually metal, cap for the fingers, used in sewing to push the needle.
watermark: A translucent design impressed on the surface of paper and visible when the paper is held to the light.
ferns: Any of a group of some twenty thousand species of vascular plants classified in the division Pteridophyta that lack seeds and reproduce by shedding spores to initiate an alternation of generations.
apostrophe: The text character ’, which serves as a punctuation mark in various languages and as a diacritical mark in certain rare contexts.
visualization: The act of visualizing, or something visualized.
desirous: Feeling desire; eagerly wishing; eager to obtain
knaves: A boy; especially, a boy servant.
pikes: A very long spear used two-handed by infantry soldiers for thrusting (not throwing), both for attacks on enemy foot soldiers and as a countermeasure against cavalry assaults.
textiles: (usually in the plural) Any material made of interlacing fibres, including carpeting and geotextiles.
gendarmes: A member of the gendarmerie, a military body charged with police duties.
talc: Originally a large range of transparent or glistening foliated minerals. Examples include mica, selenite and the hydrated magnesium silicate that the term talc generally has referred to in modern times (see below). Also an item made of such a mineral and depending for its function on the special nature of the mineral (see next). Mediaeval writers adopted the term from the Arabic.
curiouser: Tending to ask questions, or to want to explore or investigate; inquisitive; (with a negative connotation) nosy, prying.
lilt: Animated, brisk motion; spirited rhythm; sprightliness.
knockouts: The act of making someone unconscious, or at least unable to come back on their feet within a certain period of time; a TKO.
scoutmaster: An adult leader of a group of Scouts.
pillaged: To loot or plunder by force, especially in time of war.
reformation: An improvement (or an intended improvement) in the existing form or condition of institutions or practices, etc.; intended to make a striking change for the better in social, political or religious affairs or in the conduct of persons or operation of organizations.
smothers: To suffocate; stifle; obstruct, more or less completely, the respiration of something or someone.
synchronise: To cause two or more events or actions to happen at exactly the same time or same rate, or in a time-coordinated way.
underdressed: To dress in insufficiently warm clothes.
anticlimactic: Lacking climax, disappointing or ironically insignificant following of impressive foreshadowing.
buoys: A float moored in water to mark a location, warn of danger, or indicate a navigational channel.
cobweb: A spiderweb, or the remains of one, especially an asymmetrical one that is woven with an irregular pattern of threads.
debug: The action, or a session, of reviewing source code to find and eliminate errors.
equalize: To make equal; to cause to correspond in amount or degree.
gondolier: A Venetian boatman who propels a gondola.
whirrs: A sibilant buzz or vibration; the sound of something in rapid motion.
overturns: To turn over, capsize or upset.
orioles: Any of various colourful passerine birds, the New World orioles from the family Icteridae and the Old World orioles from the family Oriolidae.
paralyzes: The complete loss of voluntary control of part of a person's body, such as one or more limbs.
regaining: The act by which something is regained.
scarcity: The condition of something being scarce or deficient
simulates: To model, replicate, duplicate the behavior, appearance or properties of.
socioeconomic: Of or pertaining to social and economic factors.
straightest: Not crooked or bent; having a constant direction throughout its length.
sorghum: A cereal, Sorghum bicolor (syn. Sorghum vulgare) the grains of which are used to make flour and as cattle feed.
lampposts: The pole that holds up a light so it can illuminate a wide area, such as holds up a streetlight.
locates: To place; to set in a particular spot or position.
metastasized: (of a disease or tumour) To spread to other sites in the body; to undergo metastasis.
mothered: To give birth to or produce (as its female parent) a child. (Compare father.)
overabundance: An excess of what is needed or is appropriate.
teetering: To tilt back and forth on an edge.
hydrochloride: A compound of hydrochloric acid with an organic base such as an amine
itched: To feel itchy; to feel a need to be scratched.
lithographs: A printed image produced by lithography.
